summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of transfusion-dependent anemia, likely myelodysplastic syndrome, chronic diastolic heart failure, and long-term anticoagulation presented with diffuse abdominal pain when her hemoglobin dropped to 5.8 g/dL. She received one unit of packed red blood cells, after which her pain resolved, consistent with prior episodes. A CT scan showed no acute abdominal pathology, and lung findings initially concerning for pneumonia were reinterpreted as chronic lung changes, with a follow-up CT chest recommended in three months. Her hyponatremia improved without intervention, and she was discharged home the same day in stable condition with plans for outpatient monitoring of INR, sodium, and blood counts, and resumption of her home medications including warfarin and furosemide.
